_comment: Audit of the only multi-act path in the emulator, against the two gate clauses the
objective states. Every earlier 0-illegal / 0-unclassified figure was measured on
single-act populations; this is the chained Act 1 -> Act 2 route (retained-trace seed).
Two independent reads per run: evaluate_policy (the function that owns the
'unclassified dead end' judgement) and the decoded native terminal state.
map_option_node_types holds the four successor slots the engine advertises at the map
phase; all zero means the map genuinely has no next node.
This evidences the harness path only. The seed's Act 1 is scripted, so nothing here
says anything about policy generalisation across acts.
established: on the multi-act path too: 0 illegal actions and 0 unclassified dead ends in all 3 runs

the two Act-2 map truncations are classified empty_action_mask by evaluate_policy, and their terminal states really do advertise zero successor nodes at floor 19 -- so they are map exhaustion, not a mask/map disagreement

that makes them a DIFFERENT mechanism from the act-2 boss-exit family: same reason string, different cause (post-chain map runs out at floor 19 with 37/77 HP, versus the boss node handing the run back to Map at floor 17)
the deepest chained run (Act 2 floor 22) ends as a death inside combat at 0 HP, not as a dead end, so the frontier depth is not itself an engine dead end
not_established: why the chained Act-2 map stops offering successors after row 18: this shows that it does, not what generates it
what the Act-2 terminal node of a chained run is supposed to be -- the floor-33 arithmetic in AdvanceAfterNode was still never reached
scope: simulator_chained_demo (retained-trace seed; evidences the harness path, not policy generalisation)
